Kind: a road
Mark: breaks at a step
Step: 4
Lines: "They may never raise a level, and they may never be the reason a lower level is refused." "The state of the whole is another thing. It is held against no node. It sets where the lines stand, as Step 4 has it, and the lines are the same for every node of the whole." "This is not a judgement of the person. It is a measurement of the organism's capacity." "A level raised on who a node is, where it comes from, or what others did, is the identity-based targeting KS-32.7 names, and it fires that switch."
Place: none
Why: Steps 1–3 follow from the lines they cite, including the candidate threshold and the note that the lines are the same for every node. Step 4 does not. From a finite budget and "The organism cannot afford permanent separation without risking collapse" it follows only that organism capacity can move a node from separation to removal. The step's "so" then treats other nodes' maintenance, once summed into that capacity, as the acts of others being the reason a lower level is refused. The same note already separates those: capacity is the state of the whole, held against no node, and a level raised on what others did fires KS-32.7. The cited lines do not show that carve-out collapsing, so the inference does not follow, and the conflict rule does not save it.
